chunks: Then He opened up the high heavens, and filled them with all classes of His angels: some of them are in prostration and do not kneel up, others in kneeling position and do not stand up, some of them are in array and do not leave their position, others are extolling Allah and do not get tired. The sleep of the eyes or the slip of the intellect, or languor of the body or the effect of forgetfulness does not affect them.
Among them are those who work as trusted bearers of His message, those who serve as speaking tongues for His prophets, and those who carry to and fro His orders and injunctions.
Among them are the protectors of His creatures and guards of the doors of the gardens of Paradise.

Among them are those also whose steps are fixed on earth but their necks are protruding into the skies, their limbs are getting out on all sides, their shoulders are in accord with the columns of the Divine Throne, their eyes are downcast before it, they have spread down their wings under it, and they have rendered between themselves and all else curtains of honour and screens of power.
They do not think of their Creator through image, do not impute to Him attributes of the created, do not confine Him within abodes, and do not point at Him through illustrations.
ai.seo_question: What are the different roles and attributes of angels described in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali’s description in Nahj al-Balagha categorizes angels into distinct functional groups—such as those devoted solely to prostration or carrying revelation—reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on their ontological purity and lack of free will. This passage underscores the concept of *'ismah* (infallibility) inherent in the angelic realm, distinguishing them from humans by their constant, uninterrupted servitude and their precise adherence to Divine Command (*Amr*). The text further clarifies their epistemological stance, noting that they perceive God’s essence without attributing physical form or spatial limitations, a key theme in Shia theology regarding Divine Unity.
